title: Internationalization — Where It Stands
thesis: A deliberate bet against ICU: rather than vendor tens of MB of C++ and CLDR data, Softanza ships broad hand-tables (261 countries, 323 languages, 143 scripts, Qt-sourced), a solid engine-backed datetime core with rich Ring-side formatting, and a distinctive business/holiday calendar. That same choice leaves the CLDR crown jewels absent: no locale collation, no ICU MessageFormat or plural rules, no translation catalog, no locale-aware number/currency formatting, no timezone database (ToUTC is a no-op), and no non-Gregorian calendars.

lanes.note: 261 countries, 323 languages, 143 scripts, 495 locale abbreviations, mirrored into engine SQLite (ref_data.zig / i18n.db); Qt-sourced, native names romanized
stzDate/stzTime/stzDateTime engine-backed (datetime.zig): components, leap, add-days, diff, compare, ISO/Unix round-trips; month/year add is Ring-side; naive
~40 named formats over Qt/Unicode tokens, multi-format and natural-language epoch parsing; all Ring-side, the engine stz_date_format always emits ISO
stzCalendar: quarters, weeks, working-day arithmetic, holidays, capacity and sprint planning, heat-map; plus engine-backed stzTimeLine; pure Ring, Gregorian
Engine-backed (the L1 cutover) stz_locale_currency_iso / _symbol over 143 rows with a property test; symbol / ISO lookup only, no amount formatting
StzFormatNumber groups and rounds; Ring holds per-locale separator hints (~30 languages) but the engine formatter hardcodes US separators and never reads them
Native day and month names for 11 languages via NamesOfDaysIn / NamesOfMonthsIn; all else falls back to English; engine day_name takes no locale (L3 work)
Proleptic Gregorian only, hardcoded in datetime.zig (gregorianToJulian); no Hijri, Persian, Hebrew, Buddhist or Japanese calendars
None: datetimes are naive wall-clock; ToUTC() and ToLocalTime() are no-ops that copy the components unchanged
None: the only collate in the tree is SQLite COLLATE NOCASE (ASCII case-insensitive), not linguistic collation
None: the only plural handling is an English singular/plural pair in stzDuration; no ICU MessageFormat, no CLDR plural rules, no gender/select
None: no gettext, no .po / .mo, no message catalog anywhere in the group

standouts: Reference tables whose row coverage rivals CLDR (261 countries, 323 languages, 143 scripts)
A business/holiday calendar with sprint and capacity planning that most i18n libraries lack
An engine-backed datetime core with validated construction
gaps: A timezone database (IANA/Olson zones, offset math, DST)
Locale-aware number and currency formatting over the hint tables that already ship
Fix the datetime / date / calendar / currency C22 test-runner collision (~450 assertions)
Locale-aware collation, CLDR plural rules and a translation catalog
